note: Eddi is Saint Wilfred’s priest in Rudyard Kipling’s poem “Eddi’s Service” (1910). When no congregation arrives on a stormy Christmas night, he conducts the service for an ox and an ass.
Helleborus niger, also called black hellebore: an evergreen perennial in the buttercup family, bearing white or pink-flushed flowers in winter and early spring.

short: A stern visitor in German Christmas custom.
note: Knecht Ruprecht, literally “Servant Ruprecht,” is a German Christmas visitor who questions children about their behavior and carries gifts for the good and rods for the naughty.

sources.label: William S. Walsh: Santa Klaus traditions

short: Ebenezer Scrooge of A Christmas Carol.
note: The miser transformed by supernatural Christmas visits in Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol (1843).

short: Bob Cratchit’s young son in A Christmas Carol.
note: The frail, cheerful youngest son of Bob and Mrs. Cratchit in Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol (1843).

short: The family of Scrooge’s clerk in A Christmas Carol.
note: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge’s poorly paid clerk in Charles Dickens’s A Christmas Carol; his loving family includes his wife and their son Tiny Tim.

short: The woodcutter who discovers the forty thieves’ treasure.
note: The hero of the Arabian Nights tale “Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves,” who discovers a treasure cave opened by a magic password.

sources.label: Ali Baba, or the Forty Thieves

short: Hoffmann’s enchanted toy and Tchaikovsky’s ballet hero.
note: The toy soldier in E. T. A. Hoffmann’s The Nutcracker and the Mouse King (1816), whose adventures later inspired Tchaikovsky’s ballet.

sources.label: Berlin State Library: The Nutcracker and the Mouse King

short: The bishop of Myra associated with gift-giving.
note: A Christian bishop of Myra in Lycia, traditionally placed in the fourth century, whose legends of secret generosity helped shape later Christmas gift-giving customs.

sources.label: Catholic Encyclopedia: Saint Nicholas of Myra

short: The Norse god of fertility and prosperity.
note: Freyr or Frey, a Norse deity associated with fertility, good harvests, and peace; his possessions include the golden-bristled boar Gullinbursti.

sources.label: W. A. Craigie: The Religion of Ancient Scandinavia
